newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Computer Power says business patchy.
newsitem.headline: Computer Power says business patchy.

text.p: Computer training and services group Computer Power Group Ltd said on Wednesday it had posted a solid half year operating profit to March 31 after working within what it described as a sluggish economy.
Operating profit for the half year rose 5.2 percent over the same period last year to A$4.8 million, although net profit eased slightly to A$4.8 million from A$4.97 million.
Chief executive Peter James described revenue and business growth as patchy in some areas and quite flat in others.

Chairman Roger Allen said the result was solid, "based upon business growth within an economy which has been sluggish at times". Allen said Computer Power would pay an interim dividend of three cents against no dividend for the same period last year and expected another dividend at the end of the full year.
James said he expected the company's Asian business to grow strongly after a good performance in that sector in the half.
"The Australian and Asian services businesses are growing consistent with the sector and better than the general economies," James said.
"We are solidly positioned for any lift in economic activity having established a number of new branches."
